clue.text: Skilful at trimming top in fur

indicators.note: trimming the top of a word means its first letter is cut away

parts.note: sable is a prized dark fur

explanation.surface: Someone is good at clipping the top layer of a fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Able describes someone with the skill or competence to do something well.

clue.text: Foodstuff in a wagon operating at heart of major route

indicators.note: being at the heart of something means sitting in its middle, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first and best-known motorway, a major route north from London
a car is a wagon or vehicle
a machine that is on is operating

explanation.surface: A lorry driver carries food along the middle of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway running north from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a dried pasta, so it is a foodstuff.

clue.text: Heartless bloodsuckers climbing from takeoff

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read from bottom to top
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: ticks are parasites that feed on blood

explanation.surface: Ticks clamber off a launch pad, sounding like a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the C at the centre of TICKS, leaving TIKS; 'climbing' turns that upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, a takeoff or parody of something.

clue.text: Wet corps could show a bit of bottle

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could show something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A soaked military unit might reveal a drinking habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could show' signals rearranging WET CORPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw top is the threaded cap closing a bottle, so it is one part of it.

clue.text: Chairs a committee concerning flier's respiratory aid

indicators.note: the answer is contained in and concerns the run of words that follows over the chair's word

explanation.surface: Someone chairs a committee on a pilot's breathing apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across chAIRS A Committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds have air sacs that aid their breathing, so a flier has one as a respiratory aid.

clue.text: Those impressed by texts to play trick on the head

indicators.note: placed on the head means this piece comes first, at the top of the down answer

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
scripts are the texts actors play from

explanation.surface: People are struck by scripts that pull a fast one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' here means forced into service, as by a press gang, not admiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripts are people compulsorily enlisted, the modern form of those pressed into service.

clue.text: Cross and disturbed by a university city showing opulence

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the word are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An angry protester troubles a university town known for wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges AND into NAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu, Kubla Khan's summer capital in Coleridge's poem, stands for a place of great luxury.

clue.text: Damaged important part of set with 17

definitions.meaning: a ... leg is a lame or injured one
with the 17 answer it forms a tennis term for a rally that can win a ... in a set

explanation.definitionFit: Game means lame or injured, and a game point is a key moment in a tennis set.

clue.text: Start to bike, straight and flat races see this set off with 27?

definitions.text: races see this set off with 27?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lank hair is straight and lies flat

explanation.surface: A cycle race begins along a long flat straight.
explanation.walkthrough: With the 27 answer it makes a blank cartridge, the kind a starting pistol fires to begin a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank is the shot with no bullet that a starting pistol fires to set off a race.

clue.text: Soft drink includes joint thanks to little sizzler

indicators.note: one word includes, or holds inside it, the other

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
the hip is a joint of the body
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink with a joint in it is offered as thanks for a small sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, one that sizzles in the pan.

clue.text: Once what Costner did in "The Untouchables" with accuracy

parts.note: ex means former, once
Kevin Costner played Eliot Ness in the film, so he did act Ness

explanation.surface: A film fan remembers how precisely Costner once performed his role.
explanation.walkthrough: Kevin Costner played the agent Eliot Ness in the 1987 film The Untouchables.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is the quality of being precise, the same as accuracy.

clue.text: Benefit when carrying pole in dangerously chaotic place at 18

indicators.note: one word carries the other inside it

parts.note: for someone's sake means for their benefit
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: Someone carries a pole for safety into a dangerous place.
explanation.walkthrough: With the 18 answer it makes a snake pit, a dangerously chaotic place.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is the creature that fills the snake pit, a byword for chaos and danger.

clue.text: Harbour around port etc

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A harbour sits around a port and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges PORT ETC; 'Harbour' is the verb, to shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to shelter them, to keep them safe.

clue.text: Intro to view stated by powerful person that's not really on 16

definitions.text: powerful person that's not really on 16

indicators.note: stated means the words are said out loud and heard as another

parts.note: pay-per-view is a television service, so its introduction is pay per

explanation.surface: An introduction is said by a strongman who is a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: PAY PER (the opening of pay-per-view) said out loud gives the answer; placed on TIGER it makes a paper tiger.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger is someone who seems powerful but is in fact harmless.

clue.text: Respect is at no time free

indicators.note: set free, the letters of these words are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Respect is earned for nothing at any time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges IS AT NO TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high estimation is to respect them, a regard or esteem.

clue.text: Knight's regalia is delivered by some electronic technology on 31

indicators.note: delivered as a speech is spoken out loud

parts.note: a knight is a Sir and his outfit is his kit

explanation.surface: A knight's ceremonial dress arrives by courier, along with electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR KIT said aloud gives the answer, which goes on BOARD to make circuit board.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit board carries the electronic circuitry of a device.

clue.text: Good to have row about Australian killer at 12

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Something good comes of arguing about an Australian murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiger snake is a venomous Australian snake; 'row' looks like an argument but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed at SNAKE it makes the tiger snake, one of Australia's most venomous killers.

clue.text: Round with beer drinking very close to 9

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A round of beer is drunk very close by.
explanation.walkthrough: With BLANK it makes point-blank, meaning at very close range.
explanation.definitionFit: Point-blank range is the closest range, very close to the target.

clue.text: 17's not on if made in Grand Prix at 26 down

definitions.text: made in Grand Prix at 26 down

indicators.note: not on means the letters spelling on are taken out

parts.note: the answer to 17 across is point

explanation.surface: Something isn't acceptable if done at a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: With STOP it makes a pit stop, made by cars during a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit is where Grand Prix cars halt during a race for fuel and tyres.

clue.text: Plant in ground to be sure

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Bury a bulb in the earth to make certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges TO BE SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuberose is a fragrant flowering plant grown for perfume.

clue.text: Programme about 17:17

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: prog is short for programme
the answer to 17 is point, and N is a compass point

explanation.surface: A programme is about a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a sharp point, as on a fork.

clue.text: Exaggerate about tie

parts.note: over means about, as in arguing over something
a draw is a tied result

explanation.surface: Someone overstates the importance of a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw a description is to overstate it, to exaggerate.

clue.text: Swallow this clue for pom?

parts.note: read as an instruction, ... means turn the word mop over, which gives pom

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put up with a clue about an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: A pom is Australian slang for an English person; the answer, read as an instruction, rolls MOP backwards into POM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, something to eat.

clue.text: John has note for scrubber

parts.note: the john is American slang for a toilet, the loo
fah is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The toilet has a scrubbing brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a fibrous sponge used to scrub the skin.

clue.text: Setter has 13 across to drop rubbish in

indicators.note: to drop means letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: the answer to 13 across is protect
rot is rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: The setter wants the bin to collect rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is not the puzzle's compiler but something that makes jam set.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the gelling agent that makes jam set.

clue.text: Sully girl's name in drinking den

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
Esme is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Esme's reputation is tarnished in a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmear is to smear over, to sully or stain.

clue.text: Spirit that'll cut out juice with 15

definitions.meaning: with the 15 answer, a fault that cuts off the electric current, juice being slang for electricity

explanation.definitionFit: A short is a shot of spirit, and a short circuit cuts off the power supply.

clue.text: Up-downs cease abruptly at 26 across

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: to down a drink or pot a ball both mean sinking it, so downs are pots

explanation.surface: Ups and downs come to a sudden halt.
explanation.walkthrough: With SHORT it makes stop short, to halt suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop short is to cease suddenly, abruptly.

clue.text: Vehicle, say, with grime on back that may be drawn on with 13 down

definitions.text: that may be drawn on with 13 down

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: on its back means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eg means for example, as say does
dirt is grime

explanation.surface: A vehicle with dirt on its back may get a drawing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on back' turns EG DIRT into TRIDGE; with PAPER it makes cartridge paper, thick drawing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartridge paper is thick paper made for drawing on.

clue.text: Garment in which son leaves old singer, …

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the son's letters are taken out

parts.note: Paul Robeson was a famous bass singer of the twentieth century

explanation.surface: A garment is shed by a son who leaves an old singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Robeson was an American bass singer and actor; the clue runs on into 29 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment.

clue.text: … Nelson, is swirling round?

definitions.meaning: Nelson ... was an American singer of film musicals, so his surname follows Nelson
a swirling round of water or air, a little whirlpool

explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Eddy was a 1930s singing film star, and an eddy is a small whirlpool.

clue.text: Ring to get quotients covering gold compositions

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: covering means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: ratios are quotients, one number divided by another
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A ring gets numbers wrapped round gold musical works.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorios are large sacred musical compositions for voices and orchestra.

clue.text: Right to be knocked back in extensive draughts, say, at 8

indicators.note: knocked back means a letter is pushed further back in the word

parts.note: broad means wide, extensive

explanation.surface: Right is knocked back by large drinks of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: With GAME before it, draughts is an example of a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts is a board game, played on a chequered board.
